title: fix(core): an `operation: 'update'` action posts only its collected params, never its `patch` (objectui#12941)
body:
Fixes #12941

Clause-②: no

An `operation: 'update'` action now posts only the values collected for its declared `params` (plus the transport keys the dispatch reads: `recordId`, and the `_rowRecord` stash it strips). It never posts its declared `patch`: the platform action route applies the patch itself, from the action definition it resolves by name.

## Why

`ActionRunner.executeUpdateOperation` merged `action.patch` under the collected values and handed the result to the registered `script` dispatch as `params`. So every declarative-update button sent field values its action never declares as params (the card measured `{"recordId":…,"params":{"status":"completed"}}`). The route wrote the same values either way, because objectstack's `declarativeUpdateWrite` (in `@objectstack/runtime`, `action-execution.ts`) builds the write as `{ ...patch, ...params }` with `patch` read off the resolved declaration, never off the wire. But the runtime half, objectstack-ai/objectstack#24268 (ADR-0104 D2: refuse a param the action does not declare), would answer every such button with a 400. That half waits on this change.

Server read, done read-only at objectstack `fb6fb24e2` (the `action-execution.ts` diff to `origin/main` `53ef75243` is empty). The REST door reads `recordId` (path, else body) and `body.params`, and nothing else. It runs `enforceActionParams` on `body.params`, then `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction`, which writes `declarativeUpdateWrite(actionDef, reqParams)`. The MCP `run_action` door calls the same executor. So the console stops sending nothing the server reads. The server has applied the patch from the declaration since `@objectstack/runtime` 17.4.0, the release that first executed this action at all (its CHANGELOG entry for objectstack#14092).

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, `executeUpdateOperation`:
  - The request is `{ ...action, params: { ...collected } }`.
  - The route's merge, `{ ...patch, ...collected }`, is still computed, but only for the Undo snapshot. `writtenFields` is its keys minus `_rowRecord` and `recordId`, as before, and `redoData` reads from it. So Undo still covers the patch fields, which the route writes, and it never reads the request.
  - Doc comments that said a request without the merged patch makes the route write nothing are corrected: the `operation` field doc, the dispatch comment in `execute`, and the method doc. They now say why `operation` is still read before `type`: the Undo capture, the no-route refusal, and the unparsed row with no `type`.
- `.changeset/12941-update-action-params.md`: `@object-ui/core` patch.

No key, export or type moves. Only what the runner sends changes. No docs page describes this request body (searched `content/docs`, the package READMEs and `skills/`), so no docs change.

## The pin: a route that refuses undeclared params

New describe block in `ActionRunner.updateOperation.test.ts`, "against a route that refuses undeclared params". It runs the real `ActionRunner` and the real `createServerActionHandler` over a route stub. The stub resolves the declaration by the action name in the URL, judges the request's `params` with `@objectstack/spec`'s own `validateActionParams`, and otherwise writes `{ ...declaration.patch, ...params }`. Unlike today's runtime, it judges even an action with no declared params, which is the #24268 behaviour. The action is dispatched in the shape `ObjectGrid` hands a row action: definitions under `actionParams`, row under `params._rowRecord`.

- **A patch-only button** (`mark_done`, `patch: { status: 'done' }`): no refusal, success, and the route writes `{ status: 'done' }` to `rec_10`.
- **Control: a button that declares a param** (`add_note`, one declared `note` param): the request is exactly `{ recordId: 'rec_10', params: { note: 'typed by the user' } }`, and the route writes `{ status: 'done', note: 'typed by the user' }`.
- **Control: the stub refuses.** It is sent the old request (the patch key as a param), and refuses with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `status`. The runner reports failure with an error toast, and nothing is written. This keeps the two greens above from being vacuous.

**Ablation, run once on committed head `dea635f7`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`.** The anchor `const result = await dispatch({ ...action, params: wire }, this.context);` was replaced with `params: { ...patch, ...wire }`, which puts the patch back into the request. The tool reported the anchor going from 1 to 0 hits and the blob from `acafeae2d6d8` to `2b4441518d61`. Expected direction: red. Observed: red. 6 of 13 tests failed, including "a patch-only button writes its patch" (the route's refusals read `[{ action: 'mark_done', code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', params: ['status'], status: 400 }]`) and the declared-param control. The refusal control stayed green. Restore: the blob is back to `acafeae2d6d8`, equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and a rerun gives 13 of 13 passed. The test imports `../ActionRunner` relatively, so no `dist` is involved.

## Pins flipped to the new request body

| Pin | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ActionRunner.updateOperation.test.ts`, "POSTs … with the record id" | params `{ recordId, status }` | `{ recordId }` |
| same file, "dispatches on `operation` even when the action carries NO `type`" | `toMatchObject({ status })` | `toEqual({ recordId })` |
| same file, the "a collected value wins" case | params carried patch `status` | only `{ recordId, note }`; the route's merge is described in the comment |
| same file, the undoable capture | unchanged undo/redo values | adds that the request carries `note` alone while undo covers `status` |
| `action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx`, "`operation: update` …" (both `action:button` and `action:icon`) | dispatch params carried `stage` from patch | dispatch def carries `operation` and `patch`, and params are the supplied values only |
| `action-button-undoable-11168.test.tsx`, "on a record page" | body `params: { status: 'done' }` | `params: {}` (undo still `status`) |
| `useConsoleActionRuntime.undoLookupId-11122.test.tsx`, the route stub | wrote the params it was sent | writes `{ ...action.patch, ...params }`, as the route does |
| `undoProjectedRow-10404.test.tsx` (plugin-grid), the route stub | same | same correction |

Before the flips, those last four files failed 6 tests against the fix, which is how they were found. The other suites that author `operation: 'update'` did not need changes: `RecordDetailView.undoLookupId-11122` and `AppContent.undoFallbackObject-11080` stub the dispatch without reading the request, and the bulk paths in plugin-grid write through `bulkActionDefs`, not this runner.

## Verification (head `8502b417`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/src/actions/`: 35 files, 565 tests passed.
- Every test file under `packages`/`apps` that authors `operation: 'update'` (35 files), plus `packages/core/src/actions/` and `packages/components/src/renderers/action/`: 103 files, 1637 tests passed. This ran on the tree of `dea635f7`. The one later commit only swaps two casts in the core pin for a typed helper, and the core suite above was rerun after it.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` (both programs, the test program lists the pin file): exit 0. It needed `@object-ui/types` built first.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0 · `pnpm check:test-path-roots` 0 · `pnpm check:changeset-claims` 0 · `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0 · `pnpm changeset:check` 0 · `pnpm check:action-forward-parity` 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 6 changed TS files: 0 errors, and no warning added over base.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the diff: NOT GOVERNED.
- Declared to CI: the `tsconfig.test.json` type-check of `components`, `app-shell` and `plugin-grid`, whose test files changed. Their dependency closures were not built locally. The full farm is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- Read-only observation, not measured at a door and not filed. objectstack's `declarativeUpdateWrite` merges the request's `params` into the write whole, so a built-in key the ADR-0104 contract admits (`recordId`, `objectName`, `_selectedIds`) would land in the data-plane write bag when a client sends it inside `params`. The console's shared dispatch keeps an explicit `params.recordId` in `params` as well as at the top level, and it did so before this change too. This change neither adds nor removes that key. What the data plane does with it was not measured. The open question goes to the seat, with the objectstack half (#24268) in view.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
